correctness.rationale: For necessity, a point in an omitted exterior or interior level is squeezed by fixed retained points under any retraction; antichain incomparability forces the relevant retained boundary to be a singleton. For sufficiency, the explicit blockwise map fixes the retained subset, collapses partially retained levels internally, and sends each omitted block to an allowed singleton boundary; its target-level index is nondecreasing, with equal indices across source levels only when the common image is one point. This proves order preservation. The eventual-image statement then follows from the general finite-space equivalence between retracts and eventual images. Exhaustive replay matched the criterion for every nonempty subset in six test weak orders.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for a standard family of finite spaces, not a finite census or arbitrary slice. It converts the general but nonconstructive-looking description of eventual images as retracts into a simple levelwise criterion and an explicit retraction. Singleton levels emerge as exact gates for deleting runs of levels, giving a reusable structural description for finite-space dynamics on weak orders.
